info.title: PiglorOS Gateway
info.summary: The sole public application boundary of PiglorOS (ADR-022).
info.description: Canonical v1 contract of the Gateway (#301). Draft until Wave 9 acceptance: before then Draft fixtures may be replaced without compatibility code. Every failure is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body whose `code` is one of `problem-types.json`. That registry is open: a later v1 revision may add a problem type, so a client handles a `code` it does not know by its HTTP status and `retryable` and never fails on it; a registered `code` is never removed or renamed within v1. Every mutation that is retry-safe carries an `Idempotency-Key` header. Events are ordered by Timeline sequence, never by wall time. Response schemas are closed so that this revision detects drift; clients must ignore unknown members, because later v1 revisions may add optional ones. No operation creates a real-world effect. Operations marked `x-pigloros-status: draft` (owner `x-pigloros-owner`) are the Wave 9 resource families of #1313: they are not served, only their golden examples validate, and no served-response fixture may exercise them. `x-pigloros-limits` states the normative request and response limits (spec section 10); a `schema` limit is enforced by the named schema keywords and a `runtime` limit by the named problem; its `surface` says whether it bounds a served or a Draft operation, and its `direction` how a served limit may move within v1 (`request`: only grow, `response`: only shrink, `both`: fixed). Compatibility (#1314): the API major is the first path segment; a path under another major (such as `/v2/...`) is `400 unsupported-version`, and an unknown required schema or Event version in a request is `400 unsupported-version`, never a fallback. An execution profile the deployment cannot serve is `409 incompatible-profile`. Served operations, their response headers and security schemes, and the served limits are frozen in `compatibility/baseline.json` and stay supported through Wave 10 after Wave 9 acceptance: within v1 a change may only add optional members or accept more request values; removing or newly requiring a member, narrowing what a request accepts, widening what a response returns (except adding a problem `code`) or changing a schema identity or its declared handling of unknown members needs a new major. An open request object ignores unknown members, a closed one (`additionalProperties: false`) rejects them, and a schema-less value such as `EventView.payload` is preserved verbatim. The frozen examples under `compatibility/examples/` stay valid for the whole window.

EventCursor.description: An opaque continuation cursor bound to one Timeline and one host inventory generation. Clients pass it back unchanged; a cursor of an older generation is `append-conflict`.

IdempotencyKey.description: A caller-generated key of 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters. Repeating the key with the same request bytes returns the original result; reusing it with different bytes is `idempotency-conflict`.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem details body. `code` is the stable family of problem-types.json; `type` is its URN. `detail` is safe human-readable text whose wording is not part of the contract.

instance.description: The matched route template of the failed request; the request path only for an unrouted request.

retryable.description: Whether an identical retry may succeed later.

EventView.description: A committed Event. `seq` is its position in Timeline Order and is the commit receipt; `event_type` names its schema.

payload.description: The decoded payload when the canonical CBOR is JSON-compatible; absent otherwise.

EventPage.description: One page of committed Events in ascending Timeline Order. `next_from_seq` is null only when the Timeline is exhausted; `next_cursor` is null when the host binds no inventory generation.

WorldActionV1.description: The typed `world.action.v1` proposal. `params` are two JSON floats (X, Z, metres per second); integers are rejected at admission as `admission-rejected` (JSON Schema cannot distinguish them).

ActionRequest.description: One typed simulated action. It affects simulation state only; no route creates a real-world effect.

OwnTracksLocation.description: An OwnTracks `location` message; every other member is discarded by minimization.

AdmissionReceipt.description: The 202 answer of an asynchronous admission (Decision Preview, actions of #305/#306). It never claims that an Event committed; the committed Event receipt does.

idempotency_key_digest.description: BLAKE3 of the idempotency key; the raw key is never echoed.

bound_inputs.description: The digests of the input revisions and profile the admission binds.

CommittedEventReceipt.description: The authoritative commit receipt: the Event at its Timeline sequence and the cursor that observes its Projection.

Digest.description: A BLAKE3-256 digest in lower-case hex.

PageCursor.description: An opaque resumable cursor. Clients pass it back unchanged; a cursor of another resource, generation or inventory is `append-conflict`.

DomainKey.description: A canonical lower-case ASCII identifier (so its length in characters is its length in bytes): a capability, dimension, Plugin, rule or option key.

Label.description: Participant-authored display text without control characters. Its UTF-8 encoding is at most 128 bytes (`x-pigloros-limits.label_bytes`, enforced at admission); `maxLength` is the coarse character bound that follows from it.

ExecutionProfile.description: The ADR-104 EPF1 execution profile a resource was produced under, or its explicit absence. It never carries the serving mode, which is `mode_profile`. Until #461 installs an EPF1 every Gateway resource reports `state: unavailable` with `reason: not-installed`. When `installed`, `profile_id` is the ADR-058 family and `profile_digest` the raw EPF1 digest; the resource envelope constrains `profile_id` to the servable set of its mode.

GatewayModeProfileId.description: A Gateway execution-mode profile (GMP1, ADR-134 §1). Its namespace is disjoint from the ADR-058 `ExecutionProfileId`: neither is ever accepted where the other is expected. The profiles are composition-verified, never installed, qualified or a reproducibility claim; their public declaration is `execution-mode-profiles.json`.

ModeProfileIdentity.description: The members that identify one GMP1 binding: its kind, profile, mode, digest and store binding epoch. `mode_profile_digest` is BLAKE3(UTF-8 `PiglorOS.GatewayModeProfile.v1` || 0x00 || canonical GMP1 bytes), recomputable from `execution-mode-profiles.json`. `mode` pairs with `mode_profile_id`. The schemas that compose it close themselves.

binding_epoch.description: The store binding epoch: 1 at bind, incremented on every rotation and migration (ADR-134 §8).

ModeProfile.description: The GMP1 a resource was produced under (ADR-134 §5). A resource materialized from committed Events or stored revisions reports the binding epoch recorded in its producing commit's evidence; a resource computed per request reports the epoch current when it is computed. The history record of an epoch never changes, so the disclosure stays stable across later rotation or migration. Only Session reports the current mode.

SessionModeProfile.description: The current GMP1 binding of the serving store, with the operator's network grants and this Principal's network posture (ADR-134 §5). `network` is `absent` in Air-Gapped mode; in Local mode it is `capability-granted` only when the GMP1 allows network and the Principal holds the capability `gateway.network.v1`, otherwise `denied`. `gateway.network.v1` authorizes no operation in v1. Clients should show `network_grants` next to `network`, so an operator-exposed spectator or OwnTracks ingress stays visible when the Principal's own network is `denied`.

network_grants.description: The operator's `--network-grant` values, sorted. Air-Gapped accepts none.

ProducedUnderModeProfile.description: One GMP1 binding epoch that covers an exported commit.

binding_epoch.description: The store binding epoch: 1 at bind, incremented on every rotation and migration (ADR-134 §8).

ProvenanceReference.description: The digest of the resource's provenance record and its origin class. Provenance describes lineage only; it is not a signature, conformance or calibration claim.

Availability.description: Capability-filtered availability. Each withheld member names why it is absent, so unknown, unauthorized, deleted and unavailable stay distinct; an `available` resource withholds nothing.

ResourceEnvelope.description: The members every Draft resource carries: its schema identifier, resource ID, exactly one of an immutable `revision` or a monotonic `generation`, a provenance reference, the GMP1 `mode_profile` it was produced under (Session: the current binding), the EPF1-only `execution_profile` and capability-filtered availability. Ordering uses Timeline sequence, Fork generation and schema ordinals, never wall time. Each resource schema composes this envelope and closes itself with `unevaluatedProperties`.

revision.description: An immutable revision; a change is a new revision.

generation.description: A monotonic generation; it never decreases.

mode_profile.description: Session reports `session-mode-profile` (the current binding); every other resource reports `mode-profile` (the binding it was produced under).

LifecycleState.description: The Wave 9 state machine (spec section 7). No response collapses these states; a resource names the subset it can reach. `submitted` and `rejected` are answered synchronously: a rejection is a problem body.

ReplayClaim.description: The ADR-060 ReplayClaim, strongest first: `exact`, then `exact-authoritative-with-redacted-views` (authoritative Events and Projections still reproduce; some views are redacted), then `structural-only`, then `unverifiable-artifacts-missing`; `incompatible-profile` is orthogonal. Erasure and revocation only preserve or weaken it, so a `degraded` resource never claims `exact`. That a later generation never strengthens the claim is a runtime obligation (#307/#309); a single document cannot show it.

RevisionRef.description: One exact immutable input revision and the digest of its canonical bytes.

RevisionParent.description: The revision a new revision of the same resource derives from.

Session.description: The authenticated Principal's own session: effective grants, consent, the current execution mode (`mode_profile`, with the operator network grants and this Principal's network posture) and the EPF1 execution profile. `generation` is the authority generation; it advances on every grant, consent or revocation change.

grants.description: The effective capabilities derived by the Gateway; a client never supplies a trusted capability. The DomainKey `gateway.network.v1` is the Principal network capability (ADR-134 §4): it authorizes no operation in v1 and only decides the `mode_profile.network` disclosure; it is granted only through explicit-grant provisioning, never an operator flag.

ScenarioRoomInput.description: The participant-authored members of one ADR-041 ScenarioRoomDescriptor. Unknown members are rejected; the correlation ID and hashes are server-owned and cannot be supplied. The canonical descriptor is at most 4,096 bytes (`x-pigloros-limits.room_descriptor_bytes`).

plugins.description: Plugins already admitted and bundled by the deployment trust policy; a room cannot discover, install or retrieve a Plugin.

value_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.
A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

DeriveScenarioRoomRevisionRequest.description: A complete new descriptor derived from `parent_revision`; there is no automatic merge.

ScenarioRoomDescriptor.description: The admitted ADR-041 descriptor, the payload of one `room.revision.v1` Event.

plugins.description: Plugins already admitted and bundled by the deployment trust policy; a room cannot discover, install or retrieve a Plugin.

value_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.
A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

correlation_id.description: 16 runtime-generated non-zero bytes; never caller supplied.

ScenarioRoomRevision.description: One immutable Scenario Room revision. `id` is the room ID; `commit` is the `room.revision.v1` Event that recorded it. An identical descriptor is deduplicated to the existing revision.

CreatePreferenceRequest.description: Without `parent` it creates revision 1 of a new Preference set; with `parent` it creates the next revision of that set.

weights.description: Named dimension weights in [-1, 1] as integer micro-units; a dimension appears once (checked at admission).

PreferenceRevision.description: One immutable subject-scoped Preference revision. A revision whose subject erased it answers `deleted` to that subject and `not-found-or-unavailable` to everyone else.

weights.description: Named dimension weights in [-1, 1] as integer micro-units; a dimension appears once (checked at admission).

x_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

z_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

options.description: The user-supplied alternatives; a key appears once.

x_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

z_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

options.description: The user-supplied alternatives; a key appears once.

CreateDecisionPreviewRequest.description: Binds one inert preview to exact input revisions and one execution profile.

DecisionPreview.description: One Decision Preview. Admission (`admitted`) is never a commit claim; only `committed` names an Event sequence. `committed` is null exactly while the preview is `admitted` or `failed` (pre-commit); every later state, including `degraded`, follows a commit. Every proposal is inert and no route creates a real-world effect.

toss_up.description: True when the margin is below 0.02.

committed.description: The committed simulated action, once its Event has a sequence.

SimulatedActionRequest.description: One typed simulated ProposedAction of the preview's factual Timeline. It is authorized, approved by the host-owned ActionApprover and only then committed; it mutates simulation state only. The canonical payload is at most 4,096 bytes.

observed_seq.description: The Logical Head the client observed; a moved head is `append-conflict`.

ProjectionView.description: One page of a capability-filtered Projection at a Projection Cut. `id` is the Timeline ID and `generation` its Fork generation (0 for a factual Timeline); a quarantined generation is never served.

fold_cursor.description: The Projection Cut: the last sequence folded.

value.description: The capability-filtered state value; absent when withheld.

Intervention.description: One ordered ADR-064 Intervention. Ordinals are contiguous from 0; an Intervention cannot target consent, capability, trust, erasure or audit state.

value_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

forks.description: Ordered Forks; at least one is the explicitly labelled adversarial condition.

Ensemble.description: An ordered ensemble of generation-isolated Forks with complete endogenous suffix recomputation (ADR-064). A Fork that is not `complete` exposes no suffix digest: no partial suffix is authoritative, and an `incomplete` Fork names its failure. A `complete` ensemble has only complete Forks. Fork ordinals are unique and contiguous from 0 in array order; JSON Schema cannot express that, so the contract check enforces it on every example.

CreateReplayRequest.description: Replays one named immutable closure. A closure whose ReplayClaim is weaker than `minimum_replay_claim` is `replay-claim-insufficient`.

Replay.description: One Replay: the ADR-058 class and outcome with its ADR-060 ReplayClaim, an independent tuple. A computational match never strengthens the claim. `verified-exact` with `exact-authoritative-with-redacted-views` is coherent (the authoritative outputs matched; views are redacted), but `verified-exact` is impossible once only structural or no artifact evidence remains or the profile is incompatible. A `degraded` Replay never claims `exact`.

CalibrationStatus.description: Calibration Report status: explicitly `unavailable` or `insufficient-evidence`, otherwise a report naming its population, method and limitations. It is named empirical evidence, never general truth.

PreviewEvidence.description: Reactions, trace, uncertainty, Calibration Report status, provenance and claim strength of one preview. Evidence classes are separate members and never substitute for one another; Plugin metadata is digest-bound disclosure without Plugin authority.

reactions.description: Committed reactions in Timeline Order; `fork_ordinal` is null on the factual Timeline.

trace.description: The ADR-059 structured trace page, ordered by `ordinal`.

external_copy_acknowledged.description: The subject acknowledges that an authorized copy outside PiglorOS cannot be recalled.

Export.description: A minimized, content-addressed, subject-authorized export and its ReproManifest closure, paged by `next_cursor`. An `exported` export names its ReproManifest. Later erasure redacts managed records and weakens the ReplayClaim (a `degraded` export never claims `exact`); it does not claim that external copies vanished. `produced_under_mode_profiles` lists the GMP1 binding epochs its commits were produced under.

produced_under_mode_profiles.description: Every GMP1 binding epoch that covers an exported commit, sorted by `binding_epoch` (ADR-134 §5). The source deployment's produced-under modes travel here; an importing store records them under its own importing epoch and does not re-assert them.

ConsentRevocation.description: A recorded consent revocation. `generation` is the authority generation from which it is effective; it stops future protected work and is distinct from erasure.

impact_acknowledged.description: The subject saw the retained classes and the ReplayClaim impact.

Erasure.description: The authenticated subject's own erasure. The ADR-060 lifecycle is monotonic, a `complete` erasure has as many positive acknowledgements as required, destroyed values are never reconstructed and the ReplayClaim never strengthens: these are runtime obligations of #309 that a single document cannot show, not schema rules.

state.description: The ADR-060 lifecycle; no edge is backward.

PageCursor.name: cursor
PageCursor.description: Continuation from the previous page's cursor.

Problem.description: A failure of the problem-types.json registry.

interventions_per_fork.source: ADR-041 section 1 and ADR-064 InterventionV1; pos-core MAX_FORK_MANIFEST_INTERVENTIONS_V1

ensemble_forks.source: chosen by #1313; the acceptance ensemble is 2 (spec section 1)

identifier_length.source: pos-core MAX_AUTHORITY_TEXT_BYTES; ADR-064 owner IDs 1-128 bytes; identifiers are ASCII, so maxLength in characters is the byte bound

label_bytes.source: pos-crypto plugin_manifest MAX_LABEL_BYTES; UTF-8 bytes checked at admission, Label maxLength is only the coarse character bound

principal_concurrent_operations.source: chosen by #1313; admitted operations not yet terminal

principal_admissions_per_minute.source: chosen by #1313; an operational wall-clock quota that never decides an authoritative result

principal_denial_records_per_minute.source: apps/piglor-gateway MAX_DENIAL_RECORDS_PER_PRINCIPAL_PER_MINUTE (#1359); a fixed one-minute window that bounds durable denial evidence and never decides an authority result

denial_records_per_minute.source: apps/piglor-gateway MAX_DENIAL_RECORDS_PER_MINUTE (#1359); the host-wide bound of the same window

authority_denial_records.source: pos-core MAX_AUTHORIZATION_DENIAL_RECORDS (#1359); a full authority store refuses further denial evidence and never prunes it
